note: NECO CRS round 7 (R49 top-up): withered hand on the Sabbath; Paul's thorn in the flesh; Demetrius' silver shrines; Ehud and Eglon; Athaliah; Ebed-melech; Samson's riddle; Jotham's bramble fable; Stephanas; Ahithophel; Hiram of Tyre; Elijah and the captains of fifty; Elisha healing Jericho's water; the widow's oil; Hezekiah's sundial; Job's miserable comforters; seven churches; the 144,000; the mark of the beast 666; the four horsemen; the two witnesses; Ebenezer stone; Samuel's farewell integrity; Saul among the prophets; Joash's chest for temple repair. Scanned against the whole CRS pool (JAMB, WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the synagogue, Jesus healed a man whose right hand was withered, even though it was the Sabbath and the scribes watched to accuse him. The healing showed that
questions.B: doing good is lawful on the Sabbath
questions.C: the scribes were right to be angry
questions.D: the man had broken the law
questions.explanation: Mercy does not check the calendar first.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul pleaded three times for the removal of the 'thorn in the flesh' given to keep him from being too elated. God's answer was that
questions.A: Paul should pray a fourth time
questions.B: the thorn would be removed at once
questions.C: his grace was sufficient for Paul
questions.D: the thorn was a punishment for sin
questions.explanation: Strength, not removal, was the gift.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Ephesus, the silversmith who stirred up a riot against Paul because the gospel was ruining the trade in silver shrines was
questions.explanation: His craft, he said, was in danger from the Way.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ehud, the left-handed judge who delivered Israel from Moab, killed the fat king Eglon by
questions.B: stabbing him with a hidden dagger
questions.explanation: A left hand carried what the guards never checked.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Ahaziah's death, his mother destroyed the royal offspring of Judah and reigned herself for six years, until the boy Joash was crowned. This only queen to rule Judah was
questions.explanation: She took the throne by blood and lost it the same way.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jeremiah was lowered into the muddy cistern to die, the Ethiopian court official who pulled him out with ropes and old rags was
questions.explanation: A foreigner's kindness saved the prophet of doom.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Samson bet the Philistines thirty garments over a riddle he drew from a lion and honey: 'Out of the eater came something to eat.' The riddle was solved only because
questions.B: his wife coaxed the answer from him
questions.C: he told his companions at once
questions.explanation: She pressed him day after day until he told her.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After the men of Shechem made Abimelech king, Jotham stood on Mount Gerizim and told the fable of the trees that chose as their king
questions.explanation: The only tree that offered shadow by burning others.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul commended the household of Stephanas as the first converts of Achaia, who
questions.A: left the faith soon after their baptism
questions.B: refused to support the church at all
questions.C: sided with Paul's opponents in Corinth
questions.D: devoted themselves to serving the saints
questions.explanation: First-fruits of a province, and serving still.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: During Absalom's rebellion, David's counsellor whose wisdom was so trusted that it was said to be as the oracle of God — and who hanged himself when his advice was rejected — was
questions.explanation: The wisest head of the kingdom broke when the king no longer heard it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The king of Tyre who supplied cedar trees and craftsmen for the building of Solomon's temple, in exchange for wheat and oil, was
questions.explanation: Lebanon's cedar came to Jerusalem by his friendship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When King Ahaziah sent a captain with fifty men to arrest Elijah, the prophet called down fire from heaven that consumed them. This happened
questions.B: only once in the whole story
questions.D: twice before the third captain was spared
questions.explanation: Two companies burned; the third captain begged humbly and lived.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The men of Jericho complained that their water was bad and the land unfruitful. Elisha healed the water by
questions.explanation: A bowl of salt made the spring sweet to this day.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The widow whose two sons were about to be taken as slaves filled every vessel she could borrow with oil from one small jar, sold the oil and paid her debts, after Elisha told her to
questions.A: sell her house and land at once
questions.B: beg for alms at the city gate
questions.C: borrow empty vessels from her neighbours
questions.D: take her case before the king
questions.explanation: The oil flowed as long as a vessel waited to receive it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: As a sign that he would recover, God made the shadow on the steps of Ahaz go back
questions.explanation: The sundial ran backward for the dying king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Job called his friends who came to comfort him in his suffering
questions.explanation: They came to console him and ended accusing him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the book of Revelation, the risen Christ instructs John to write to the churches of Asia, among them Ephesus, Smyrna, Sardis, Laodicea and
questions.explanation: Seven lampstands, seven letters to seven cities.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the book of Revelation, the servants of God who are sealed on their foreheads before the winds of destruction are released number
questions.explanation: Twelve tribes, twelve thousand from each.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The number 666 in the book of Revelation is
questions.explanation: It marks those who follow the beast instead of the Lamb.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the book of Revelation, the Lamb opens the seals and four horsemen ride out — white, red, black and pale — carrying conquest, war, famine and
questions.explanation: The pale horse and its rider are named Death.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the book of Revelation, the two olive trees and lampstands who prophesy and cannot be harmed by fire until they finish their testimony are
questions.explanation: For three and a half days no enemy could silence them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After the Lord had helped Israel to victory over the Philistines at Mizpah, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Jeshanah and called its name
questions.A: Ebenezer, saying 'thus far the Lord has helped us'
questions.D: Gilgal, saying 'the reproach is rolled away'
questions.explanation: The stone of help remembered every battle past.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At his farewell, Samuel asked Israel to testify against him: whose ox or donkey had he taken, or whom had he defrauded? The people answered that
questions.A: he had taken nothing from anyone
questions.D: his sons must repay the people
questions.explanation: A lifetime in office without a single petition against him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the people saw Saul prophesying among the prophets, they asked in wonder
questions.explanation: The proverb is repeated to this day.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the temple repairs had long been neglected, the priests were commanded to put a chest with a hole in its lid beside the altar, into which the people
questions.A: dropped money for the house of the Lord
questions.D: kept the scrolls of the law
questions.explanation: The chest filled, and the house was repaired.
